summary: Frontend E2E testing of Lot SSO Navixy fail-closed (scenarios 1-6). Tested: real fail-closed SSO flow via ?session_key=fake..., no auto-login after failure, direct login regressions (superadmin + admin client), new console role selector, and direct API curl checks on /api/auth/navixy/exchange. 5/6 scenarios PASS. 1 CRITICAL FAIL: the amber sso-error banner never appears on /login because the axios 401 response interceptor performs a hard window.location.assign('/login'), which wipes the React ssoError state.

ui_bugs.issue: After a failed SSO exchange (401 on /api/auth/navixy/exchange), the global 401 interceptor calls window.location.assign('/login') -> full page reload -> AuthContext ssoError state destroyed -> data-testid=sso-error banner is NEVER rendered (count=0 measured). User lands on a blank login screen with no explanation, which is exactly the confusing UX the fix intended to remove. Fix: exclude '/auth/navixy/exchange' from the interceptor redirect (like /auth/login and /auth/change-password), or persist the SSO error message across the reload (e.g. sessionStorage flag / navigate via react-router).

issues: Uses a native HTML <select> (browser default styling) instead of the shadcn Select used elsewhere - visual inconsistency, cosmetic only; functionality works

action_items: Whitelist /auth/navixy/exchange in the axios 401 response interceptor (or persist the SSO error) so the amber sso-error banner is actually displayed on /login after a failed SSO exchange.
critical_code_review_comments: lib/api.js l.34-37: the 401 interceptor unconditionally hard-redirects, defeating any component-level 401 error rendering; the exclusion list must include /auth/navixy/exchange.
AuthContext heartbeat useEffect (l.81-92) has ssoSessionKey (module-level mutable, non-reactive) in its condition but not in deps; works today because user changes at the same time, but fragile.

rca_of_the_issue: Root cause of missing sso-error banner: /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js response interceptor (l.30-40) triggers setToken(null) + window.location.assign('/login') for ANY 401 except /auth/login and /auth/change-password. The failed SSO exchange returns 401, so a full browser navigation occurs and the React state (ssoError set in AuthContext catch block) is lost before Login.jsx can render it. Reproduced twice: framenavigated log shows 4 navigations to /login and sso-error locator count = 0.
